items.title: 68429_Walter P. Thomas oral history interview
items.q: So Mr. Drury patiently would sit down with me and helped me write my Valedictorian speech.

ctx.x: He was right. And all the other languages.

Right. And then another thing that he did for me... Here I am, valedictorian. So evidently, he knew that I didn't know too much about being a valedictorian. At first I didn't know what a valedictorian was. I found later that I was the one that had the highest grade from the Freshman to the Senior class in the same class. Because one boy had higher grades than me, but he had missed one year out, and he came in on our class. But originally, he was supposed to be a class ahead of us. Ralph Waller. So Mr. Drury…

Now, he was also our Economics teacher and our Public Speech teacher. These were three of the classes we had a chance to study in high school! And man, that was a privilege, when you think of it. Because some of them... Economics, you don't generally get it until you get to college. And to this day, they taught us things in Economics...
